case_name: Union Of India And Ors. v Nitdip Textile Processors Private Limited and others
holding: The power of the Legislature to classify is of wide range and flexibility so that it can adjust its system of taxation in all proper and reasonable ways.
A power to classify being extremely broad and based on diverse considerations of executive pragmatism, the Judicature cannot rush in where even the Legislature warily treads.

Discrimination resulting from fortuitous circumstances arising out of particular situations, in which some of the tax payers find themselves, is not hit by Art. 14 if the legislation, as such, is of general application and does not single them out for harsh treatment.
